question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Stick to one’s guns
solution:
The correct answer is: **To remain faithful to**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Stick to one's guns"** means to remain determined, resolute, or faithful to one's beliefs, decisions, or actions despite opposition or criticism. (अपने विचारों या निर्णयों पर दृढ़ रहना)

 
 
• **Example: **Despite the criticism from his colleagues, he decided to stick to his guns and continue with his original plan.
 
 
 
• **"To remain faithful to"** refers to staying loyal or true to someone or something. (वफादार रहना)
 
 
• **Example: **She remained faithful to her principles, even when it was difficult.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. 'To remain faithful to'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To shoot at **(गोली चलाना): To fire a gun at someone or something.

 
 
• **Example:** The soldier was ordered to shoot at the target.
 
 
 
• **To become a rebel **(विद्रोही बनना): To oppose or defy authority or tradition.
 
 
• **Example: **He decided to become a rebel and fight against the unjust system.
 
 
 
• **To become unfaithful to** (अवफादार होना): To stop being loyal or faithful.
 
 
• **Example:** She feared he would become unfaithful to her.
